info.title: stats api
info.description: The HTTP contract of the api Worker. Generated by `pithy contract`. Do not edit by hand.

get.summary: Report liveness, and which build is answering.

200.description: Liveness, and which build is answering.

status.description: Always `ok`: an answer at all is the liveness signal.

version.description: The Cloudflare version id of the build answering, or null where the Worker cannot say.

schema.description: Liveness, and which build is answering.

get.summary: Read the status of every declared secret, never a value.

200.description: The status of every declared secret, and any whose stored rows would not decode.

backend.description: Where the value lives. Decides what a null `createdAt` means.

valueType.description: How the value is interpreted: `text` or `json`.

rotatable.description: Whether a value-rotator may manage it. Never changes what is reported.

kind.description: Replaced by producing a new value the same way it was minted. Every `origin.kind: "minted"` secret, and nothing else — if the kit can make one it can make another.

oneOf.description: Rotated by the kit, on its own. The tag carries everything; there is nobody to call.

kind.description: Replaced by calling the issuer, which returns the new value. The kit cannot invent this call; the capability or the adopter supplies it, and it changes state in somebody else's system.

documentation.description: What the call does, for an operator deciding whether to trust it with a live credential.

oneOf.description: Rotated by calling the issuer. The new value comes back from somebody else's system.

kind.description: A human, in a console. No API returns the new value — a GitHub or Google OAuth client secret. This is a real answer, not a missing one.

documentation.description: The page where it is done.

oneOf.description: Rotated by a human, in a console. A real answer, and the page is the whole help.

anyOf.description: How this secret is replaced, declared separately from `origin` because neither follows from the other: a GitLab token is `obtained` and rotates by `provider`, while an OAuth client secret is `obtained` and rotates only by `manual`. Declared per secret, never per issuer — some Cloudflare secrets roll and some do not.

rotation.description: How this secret is replaced: `local`, `provider`, or `manual` — with the issuer, and the page a human goes to. Null when the registry declares nothing, which is not the same as `manual`. **This is the field a client branches on to decide whether a rotation control exists at all**, and it is metadata by construction: a kind, an issuer and an `https:` documentation URL are all it can hold. An issuer this client has never heard of parses as `other` rather than failing, so a Worker newer than its reader still renders.

keyVersion.description: Which master-key version the stored envelope sits under, or null when nothing is stored here.

createdAt.description: When it was first written to this store, ISO-8601; null when it is not stored here.

updatedAt.description: When its value was last written, ISO-8601; null when it is not stored here.

lastRotatedAt.description: The newest successful rotation, ISO-8601, or **null for never rotated** — not zero, and not the epoch.

lastFailure.description: The newest closed rotation attempt, when it failed — the field an unattended rotation is reported through (#602). Null when the newest closed attempt succeeded or none is recorded. Absent from a Worker older than the field.

at.description: When the failed attempt closed, ISO-8601.

anyOf.description: Why a rotation row closed failed, as a code. `roll-failed`, `not-recorded` and `not-rotated` are a value rotation's. `at-rest-incomplete` and `at-rest-unconfirmed` are the whole-store master-key rotation's. `not-retired` is an unattended value rotation that landed and kept the previous version, because a value sealed under it at rest was not re-encrypted. `field-key-overdue` is a field-key version still live when the next rotation came due, `field-key-ceiling` a rotation refused at four live versions, `field-key-unconfirmed` a field-key write the binding never showed, and `field-key-incomplete` a field-key pass that did not finish (#390).

reason.description: Why, as a code. Null when the failure is in words this release does not write.

anyOf.description: The newest closed attempt's failure: an instant and a code.

rotationCount.description: How many rotation attempts are recorded, successful or not.

rotateEveryDays.description: The cadence the registry declares for this secret, or null when it declares none.

overdue.description: Whether it is past that cadence. Null when the question has no answer, which is not the same as no.

items.description: One secret's status as a client reads it. Metadata only — this shape cannot express a value.

secrets.description: Every named secret the composed Worker declares, by name. Keyed entries are excluded.

unreadable.description: Declared secrets whose stored rows would not decode, by registry name — so one bad row costs its own entry and names itself, instead of costing the read (#387). Registry names only: keyed entries are excluded from this read, so no stored `<keyspace>/<key>` name can appear here. Carries no reason; why a row is malformed is a question for the database, not for a client.

schema.description: The status of every declared secret, and any whose stored rows would not decode.

get.summary: Read one secret's rotation history, newest first.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The secret to read — the `:name` path segment, matched exactly against the composed registry. A name no capability declares is a 404, not an empty history.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many rotation rows to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to a page a screen can render.

200.description: One secret's rotation history, and how much of the page would not decode.

name.description: The secret this history belongs to, echoed so a client can label it.

startedAt.description: When the rotation attempt began, ISO-8601.

completedAt.description: When it finished, ISO-8601; null while it is still running.

trigger.description: What caused it: `cron`, `manual`, or the `baseline` marker on first write.

rotatedBy.description: Who or what initiated it — a workflow instance id, an operator id, or `baseline`.

failure.description: Why a `failed` attempt failed, as a code — never the failure's text. Null when it did not fail, or failed in words this release does not write; absent from a Worker older than the field (#602).

anyOf.description: Why a rotation row closed failed, as a code. `roll-failed`, `not-recorded` and `not-rotated` are a value rotation's. `at-rest-incomplete` and `at-rest-unconfirmed` are the whole-store master-key rotation's. `not-retired` is an unattended value rotation that landed and kept the previous version, because a value sealed under it at rest was not re-encrypted. `field-key-overdue` is a field-key version still live when the next rotation came due, `field-key-ceiling` a rotation refused at four live versions, `field-key-unconfirmed` a field-key write the binding never showed, and `field-key-incomplete` a field-key pass that did not finish (#390).

items.description: One rotation attempt as a client reads it. A failure is a status and a code, never a message.

rotations.description: Its rotation attempts, newest first, capped by `limit`.

unreadable.description: How many rows in this page would not decode (#387). A count and not a list, because every row here is the same secret's and what identifies one is its place in the history — which is exactly what a row with an undecodable `startedAt` cannot supply. Reported so a client can say the history is incomplete rather than render a short list as a whole one.

schema.description: One secret's rotation history, and how much of the page would not decode.

post.summary: Rotate one secret inside this Worker, for the environment the credential names.
post.description: Takes no body. The successor is minted or fetched inside the Worker and never returned; the answer says what happened, not what the value is.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The secret to read — the `:name` path segment, matched exactly against the composed registry. A name no capability declares is a 404, not an empty history.

name.description: The secret that was rotated, echoed so a client can label the result.

status.description: How it ended: `rotated`, `unchanged`, `unrecorded`, or `failed`. `unrecorded` is the one that needs a human in a console now — read it before `recorded`.

kind.description: How the registry says this secret is replaced — the same fact `rotation.kind` reports on a status read.

rolled.description: Whether the issuer's credential was actually replaced. True only for a `provider` rotation that reached its rotator; a `local` mint rolls nothing anywhere.

rollFailed.description: Whether the **rotator itself** threw, rather than the store after it. With `rolled`, this is the difference between *was rolled* and *may have been rolled*: a call that reached the issuer and lost its answer cannot be told from one that never landed, and a report claiming either is wrong half the time about the fact being acted on. False on every run that never called a rotator.

recorded.description: The environments this run wrote the new value to, in the order each write landed.

stranded.description: The environments the new value never reached. Empty on a run that finished. With `rolled` true these hold a credential the issuer has already retired.

anyOf.description: Why a rotation did nothing. `manual` — the secret declares that only a human in the issuer's console can replace it, so there was nothing to call. `dry-run` — the operator asked what would happen. Both are answers rather than failures, and both exit zero.

reason.description: Why nothing was called, when nothing was — `manual` for a secret only a human can replace. Null whenever something was attempted.

attempts.description: How many store attempts the failing environment cost. Null when nothing was stored.

rotation.description: The outcome. One secret per call, so there is no summary line to hide a partial failure behind.

get.description: The home page strip. Cached until the next file is ready, 15 minutes after the 02:00 UTC run starts, by default, or for five minutes once that file is late, then revalidated in the background for an hour. `nextUpdate` is the ready time of the run after this file, so a copy may revalidate before it.

parameters.name: if-none-match
parameters.description: ETags this API answered before, or `*`. When one still matches, the answer is a 304 with no body. A value that is not an entity-tag list is ignored.

200.description: The home page strip's headline numbers, served at `/v1/summary`. Nothing in it needs the history.

nextUpdate.description: The time the next run after this file is ready: the first collector run to start after `generatedAt`, ready 15 minutes after the 02:00 UTC run starts, by default. A cache may revalidate sooner: at the current run's ready time, or after five minutes while a run is late.

releases.description: The kit's release history, null before the registry is read.

issues.description: Issues on the kit's repository, null before GitHub is read.

total.description: Every bug: an issue typed Bug or labelled `bug`.

stars.description: Stargazers, null before GitHub is read.

tests.description: Tests in the kit, null until they are counted.

Error.description: The body of every error response.
Any failure. The status is the error's own; the body is always this shape.

bearer.description: A session token from `@pithy-sh/auth`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: the one sign-in returns, then the `refreshToken` each `/token/rotate` answers with. The rotation's `accessToken` is a JWT for services outside the Worker, and these routes refuse it.

session.name: better-auth.session_token
session.description: A browser session cookie from `@pithy-sh/auth`, named `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` over HTTPS. A state-changing request also needs its `Origin` to be one the Worker trusts.
